what_happened: On a multi-lane highway with a STRAIGHT/RIGHT command, the policy planned a lane change to the left that the human never made, and sped up from 4.2 to 6.0 m/s. It cut into the adjacent left lane and its front hit actor 56, which was travelling alongside and slightly ahead in that lane.

The ego was cruising straight on the freeway at about 8 m/s with a clear gap of over 24 m ahead. Actor 33 came up from behind in the lane to the left and, as it passed, its right side touched the ego's front-left corner. The ego was only 0.9 m off the recorded human path, so it is unclear whether the ego drifted slightly left into the passing car or the replayed car squeezed it; the smear in the camera happens only at the moment of impact.

After handoff the policy planned and steered a lane change to the left on a straight multi-lane highway, while the route said STRAIGHT and later RIGHT. It cut into the next lane while vehicle 56 was right beside it there, and the ego's front-left corner hit 56 at about 6 m/s.

On a straight multi-lane highway, the policy planned a lane change to the left when it should have stayed in its lane. It sped up from 4.2 to 6.0 m/s and steered into the lane where vehicle 56 was driving alongside it, hitting that car with its front-left corner.

On a multi-lane freeway with the STRAIGHT command, the policy planned a drift to the left (orange path) instead of following the recorded straight path (green line). It moved about 0.9 m left, and its front corner hit actor 33, which was coming up in the adjacent left lane. The lead vehicle stayed about 25 m ahead the whole time, so this was not a following failure.

After handoff, with the command at STRAIGHT and then RIGHT, the policy planned and began a lane change to the left at about 8 m/s. It moved into the adjacent left lane just as vehicle 33 was coming up from behind on the left, and the two collided side by side at 6.2 s. There was no slow lead vehicle; the gap ahead stayed around 25 m.

The ego was replaying the logged human path (0.0 m off the recording) at about 14 m/s. Actor 36 came up from directly behind in the same lane and drove through the ego's box, ending up overlapping its front. Because the replayed actor and the ego were in the same space, this was scored as a front collision at 4.7 s, the same moment as handoff, so the policy never had a chance to act.

The ego was still replaying the recorded drive straight down its lane at about 14 m/s, with no offset from the log, when actor 16 came up from directly behind in the same lane at 3.7 s. By 4.7 s, the moment the policy took over, actor 16 overlapped the ego's front and was scored as a front collision. The policy never had control before contact, so this looks like the replayed actor driving through the ego's box, not a policy error.

The ego was going straight at about 14 m/s, still replaying the recorded drive. Actor 16 was right behind it at 3.7 s, and by 4.7 s it had driven up through the ego and overlapped its front (1.6 m gap), which the metrics counted as a front collision. This happened at the exact moment of handoff (4.7 s), so the policy never had control before the contact.

After handoff, the ego slowed from 6.5 to 3.1 m/s. It drifted about 1.4 m left of the recorded path, into the lane of actor 23, a slow vehicle just ahead-left, and hit it with its front at 7.8 s (the gap ahead had shrunk to 4.4 m). Actor 23 was heavily smeared in the camera the whole time, but it was still recognisable as a car. The ego was also rear-ended at some point.

Before the policy took over, actor 9 came up from behind in the ego's lane and hit its rear (rear collision at 3.7 s, while the ego was still replaying the log at about 5 m/s). By the 4.7 s handoff, actor 9 was driving through the ego's box, so the overlap got flagged as a front, at-fault collision at the first moment the policy was in control. The camera smear in that frame comes from the overlap.

Actor 9 came up from behind in the ego's lane and was already hitting the ego's rear at 3.7s (collision_rear=1), before the policy took over at 4.7s. It kept going through the ego, so by 4.7s it covered the ego's front and a front collision was logged at the handoff instant. Nothing was ahead in the lane (the lead was about 44 m away), so the ego was hit by a replayed actor and had no time to react.

The ego was driving straight in its lane on the recorded path while actor 9 came up fast from behind. Actor 9 hit the ego's rear by 3.7s, before the policy took over, then drove through the ego, so by 4.7s it fully overlapped the ego and a front collision was registered.

The ego was driving straight in its lane, replaying the recorded trajectory (0.0 m off) and speeding up gently, with the nearest car ahead 25–44 m away. Actor 9 came up from behind: it was already touching the ego's rear at 3.7 s, a second before handoff, and by 4.7 s it had driven through the ego and overlapped its front. That overlap is why a front collision was flagged at the moment of handoff, and the 0.5 m "gap ahead" is actor 9, not a lead vehicle.

On a congested highway, the ego drifted left out of its lane, away from the recorded path, even though the route command was STRAIGHT and then RIGHT. Its front hit actor 23, a slow vehicle in the adjacent left lane, at about 3 m/s. The rear contact recorded in the run came after this.

After handoff, the ego slowed and drifted left across the lane line even though the command was RIGHT. Its front hit the rear of actor 23, which was driving normally in the adjacent left lane ahead (gap about 4.4 m, ego at 3 m/s).

On the multi-lane highway, actor 23 cut in from the left into the ego's lane just ahead. The ego was told to go RIGHT and its plan pointed right, but it stayed in its lane (the human had already moved one lane right), braked only gently (3.7→2.9 m/s while the gap fell from 7.7 to 4.4 m), and its front hit 23. It was also rear-ended at some point.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego drove unusually slowly (about 4–5 m/s) while its planned path veered left of the route, drifting about 1.6 m off the recorded trajectory toward the left lane line. Vehicle 29 was passing on the left, and the ego sideswiped it (lateral collision) at 11.8 s.

On a straight highway with a STRAIGHT command, the ego was going only about 4 m/s and its plan kept bending left of the recorded path, so it drifted across the lane line into the lane on its left. A small vehicle (actor 29, which looks like a motorcycle) came up in that lane from behind and was hit by the ego's front-left corner.

On a multi-lane highway, the ego was going slowly (about 4–5 m/s) and its planned path wandered to the left, so it ended up about 1.5 m off the recorded human path. A small actor (29) passing in the adjacent left lane then side-swiped the ego's front-left corner, which was logged as a lateral at-fault collision with no braking issue for a lead vehicle.

The ego was moving slowly on a multi-lane highway, about 4–5 m/s. Its planned path bent left, and it drifted across the lane line toward the left lane. While it was straddling the line, its front-left corner hit actor 29, a small vehicle passing in the adjacent left lane.
